components.title: Approved architecture decision record for Vault

requirements.requirement: Applications MUST reference secrets by name `<tenant>/<path>`; request messages MUST NOT carry secret values.
The wire response to RESOLVE MUST carry a lease handle and MUST NOT carry plaintext.
Every wire request MUST be authenticated before any scope, quota or provider interaction.
Authorization MUST be deny-by-default and require role, tenant and scope membership.
Missing and unauthorized secrets MUST be externally indistinguishable.
Scope MUST be re-evaluated at use time.
A principal MUST NOT resolve, rotate or scope a secret outside its tenant namespace.
A lease MUST be bound to the resolving subject; use by any other subject MUST fail.
Use after expiry, revocation or version retirement MUST fail.
Leases MUST NOT survive a process restart (fail closed).
Rotation MUST add a version; existing leases MUST stay bound to their version.
Rotation MUST be idempotent per (subject, idempotency_key); key reuse with a different request MUST fail with CONFLICT.
No secret value MAY appear in audit, logs, metrics, traces, errors or snapshots.
Every security decision MUST produce a hash-chained audit record with reason, policy digest and config digest.
Time decisions MUST use a monotonic clock and fail closed on rollback, including quota accounting.
Only RETRYABLE outcomes MAY be retried, bounded by attempts and deadline.
Provider outage MUST deny (offline-deny) unless stale serving is configured, in which case responses MUST be marked DEGRADED and audited.
Writes MUST NOT fail over to a replica.
Operators MUST be able to freeze by global/tenant/secret/op scope; frozen operations MUST be DENIED.
Configuration MUST validate before activation, reject credential material, and keep a rollback target.
Provider transport MUST be TLS ≥ 1.2 with hostname verification outside the loopback test lane.
Request size, in-flight concurrency, per-workload rate, lease table, cache and metric series MUST be bounded.
